treatment.name: Painless Root Canal Treatment (RCT)
treatment.overview: RCT saves an infected or painful tooth by cleaning the canals, removing bacteria, and sealing them to prevent reinfection.

types.name: Anterior (Front Tooth) RCT
description: Typically single canal; faster and simpler.

types.name: Premolar/Molar RCT
description: Multiple canals; requires advanced shaping and sealing.
Often followed by a protective crown.

cost.note: Depends on tooth position, infection, and number of canals.

during: Local anesthesia; canals cleaned and shaped.
Temporary filling if multi-visit; final obturation then restoration.
after: Crown recommended to prevent fracture—especially for molars.

avoid: Chewing hard foods on the treated tooth until final crown
prefer: Soft diet for 24-48 hours after appointments
foodGuidelines.tip: Resume normal diet after final restoration unless advised otherwise.

pros: No immediate treatment cost or appointments
cons: Risk of tooth loss and spread of infection
prosConsOfSkipping.summary: RCT preserves your natural tooth, relieves pain, and prevents complications.

faq.a: With modern anesthesia, RCT is very comfortable; temporary soreness can occur after.

faq.q: Do I always need a crown?
faq.a: Crowns are strongly advised for back teeth to prevent fractures.
